scores.reason: Random plasma C-peptide with concurrent glucose is a standard, widely offered laboratory test with no timed protocol. A reference measurement system exists, but routine methods disagree most at higher concentrations and recalibration with real serum was needed; the 'low' end that matters here (about 0.2 nmol/L) is less affected than the high end. Measure type: C-peptide (random, unstimulated).
sources: PMID 38549041 DOI 10.1093/clinchem/hvae034 abstract (full text read in project: analysis/clinical-chemist.md)

scores.reason: Blood C-peptide is a standard test, but the MODY triage evidence rests on post-meal urinary C-peptide:creatinine ratio, which needs a timed sample (2 h after the largest meal) collected in boric acid and, in the cited studies, mailed to a reference laboratory; urine C-peptide is not a standardized routine assay. Score reflects the timed protocol and unstandardized urine measure. Measure type: C-peptide (blood, or post-meal urine ratio).

Insulin and C-peptide are standard immunoassays (3 on their own, but insulin is poorly standardized between methods and degrades if separation is delayed), and the sample must be drawn during hypoglycaemia (spontaneous or fasting test). The discriminating test, the sulfonylurea/meglitinide screen, is a specialised LC-MS/MS send-out (1) and can miss newer agents. Scored 2 as the limiting combination. Measure type: fasting/spontaneous-hypoglycaemia insulin and C-peptide plus drug screen.
sources: PMID 38549041 DOI 10.1093/clinchem/hvae034 abstract (insulin inter-lab CV 22.2% single measurements)
scores.correction: Applied 2026-10-23 from rescoring proposal RS-D4 (clarifications 25 to 29, user approved): Clar. 25: score the limiting assay. The drug screen is a specialised send-out and can miss newer agents (V3 own reading: 1). Insulin and C-peptide immunoassays are standard US laboratory tests [3 on availability; method differences in insulin, inter-lab CV 22.2% per PMID 38549041, argue for 2-3]. The critical-sample timing that V3 used to reach 2 is D5. Older-generation assay data are part of the sources; confidence capped at medium (clar. 20). Proposal confidence medium.

scores.reason: Fasting C-peptide is a standard test, but the criterion also uses glucagon-stimulated C-peptide (timed protocol, peak at about 6 min in the cited schemes) and must be done weeks to months after the DKA episode, with autoantibodies. Cutoffs (0.33 nmol/L fasting, 1.5 ng/mL peak) come from single-centre cohorts and assay-specific values. Measure type: C-peptide (fasting and glucagon-stimulated).

Single fasting serum C-peptide against a fixed cutoff (<0.6 ng/mL) is a standard laboratory test with no timed protocol. The cutoff is a Japanese expert criterion not tied to a named assay; between-method differences mean it may not transfer to a given US platform. Measure type: fasting C-peptide.
sources: PMID 38184802 DOI 10.1111/jdi.14121 abstract (project: full text read by skeptic)

scores.reason: Components are routine (OGTT, C-peptide, glucose), but the prognostic scores (Index60, AUC C-peptide, oral minimal model) need 5 to 9 timed samples and calculated indices that are not reportable laboratory products, with cohort-specific thresholds and no cross-assay calibration. Close to research-only for the indices (1), scored 2 because the underlying assay and OGTT are widely available. Measure type: post-load (OGTT) C-peptide with glucose.

The critical sample (glucose, BOHB, FFA, insulin, C-peptide, GH, cortisol) has to be drawn at the time of hypoglycaemia, in small paediatric volumes, with a high-sensitivity insulin assay because insulin is often below detection even in hyperinsulinism. Insulin immunoassays are not standardized between methods, and delay to separation lowers insulin and C-peptide. Individual analytes are routine, so not lower than 2. Measure type: spontaneous-hypoglycaemia (critical sample) insulin and C-peptide.
sources: PMID 37454648 DOI 10.1159/000531766 abstract (guideline; table values from project full-text read)

scores.reason: Igls grading uses basal and stimulated (mixed-meal or glucagon) C-peptide against the patient's own pre-transplant value, so it needs a timed protocol, serial measurements on one platform and sensitive assays for low values (the consensus notes low levels are detectable with sensitive assays despite graft failure). Kidney function confounds interpretation. Measure type: C-peptide (basal and stimulated).
sources: PMID 29528967 DOI 10.1097/tp.0000000000002158 abstract (project: full text read by skeptic, PMC5867272)

anchor_issues: D4 row 3: the use case bundles two measurements of different standing (insulin/C-peptide immunoassay = 3; drug screen send-out = 1). Chose 2 as the limiting combination.

D4 rows 49, 32, 10: anchor 2 combines 'unstandardized' and 'needs a timed protocol', but the rubric (rule 20) says protocol burden belongs to D5. Scored 2 for timed-protocol rows because the anchor names it; D5 should not double-count.
D4 row 49: derived indices (Index60, minimal model) sit between 'research only' (0/1) and a timed protocol (2); chose 2 with low confidence.
D4 row 7: blood C-peptide (3) and urine C-peptide:creatinine ratio (specialised, 1-2) differ; scored the evidence-backed UCPCR form as 2.

D4 general: anchors 3 and 2 do not say how to treat a standard test whose results differ by method and whose cutoffs are assay-specific; chose 3 when a single value is read against a fixed cutoff at a non-critical concentration range and 2 when a protocol is also required.
assumptions: No US-assay-specific data (FDA-cleared C-peptide or insulin immunoassay performance, proficiency-testing data) were retrieved; scores rely on multi-method and mostly pre-2020 or non-US data (Little 2008, Wiedmeyer 2007, Zhou 2022 China, Deng 2023 China), so confidence is capped at medium per clarification 20.
C-peptide and insulin immunoassays are assumed to be offered by US reference and hospital laboratories (general knowledge, not verified by a search in this run).
Sulfonylurea screening is assumed to be a send-out or specialised LC-MS/MS test in most US hospitals; PMID 26790752 describes an in-house emergency-department assay at one centre.
Biological variation of C-peptide was not searched; D4 does not depend on it.
